extracted.intended_audience: astronomers and mathematicians determining comet orbits; observational astronomers and instrument-makers
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric and observational procedures for deriving a comet's trajectory (here assumed parabolic) from discrete celestial observations, including interpolation of intermediate positions, choice and repetition of observations, graphical constructions, instrument practice, and physical interpretation of cometary tails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-difference interpolation of ordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Collige perpendiculorum AH, BI, CK, &c. differentias primas per intervalla perpendiculorum divisas b, 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b; secundas per intervalla bina divisas c, 2c, 3c, 4c, &c. tertias per intervalla terna divisas d, 2d = ... & sic deinceps; id est ita ut sit b = {AH - BI} ÷ HI, 2b = {BI - CK} ÷ IK, 3b = {CK - DL} ÷ KL &c. dein c = {b - 2b} ÷ HK ... Inventis differentiis, dic AH = a, - HS = p, p in - IS = q, q in + SK = r, r in + SL = s, s in + SM = t; pergendo scilicet ad usque perpendiculum penultimum ME, & erit ordinatim applicata RS = a + bp + cq + dr + es + ft, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use successive finite differences (first, second, third, etc.) computed over unequal intervals to interpolate the ordinate (distance from a fixed line) at an intermediate abscissa. Follow the formula RS = a + b p + c q + d r + e s + f t ... to obtain the ordinate at the desired intermediate point; the page gives the explicit definitions for b, c, d in terms of neighboring measured perpendiculars and interval lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic approximation for areas (quadrature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc areæ curvarum omnium inveniri possunt quamproximè. Nam si curvæ cujusvis quadrandæ inveniantur puncta aliquot, & Parabola per eadem duci intelligatur: erit area Parabolæ hujus eadem quam proximè cum area curvæ illius quadrandæ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several points of a quadrant of any curve are known, draw the parabola through the same points; the area of that parabola approximates the area of the original curve-quadrant. Parabola can be squared geometrically by known methods; use this parabolic approximation for estimating areas (and thereby times/areas related to motion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine intermediate comet positions by curve-fit + interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex observatis aliquot locis Cometæ invenire locum ejus ad tempus quodvis intermedium datum. Si per puncta A, B, C, D, E duci intelligatur curva regularis ABCDE; & per Lemma superius inveniatur ejus ordinatim applicata RS, erit RS longitudo quæsita.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit a regular curve through observed comet positions (A,B,C,D,E) and apply the finite-difference interpolation (Lemma VI) to obtain the comet's longitude at an intermediate time. The same method applies to latitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of observations required depends on magnitude of observed differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Si longitudinum observatarum parvæ sint differentiæ, puta graduum tantum 4 vel 5; suffecerint observationes tres vel quatuor ad inveniendam longitudinem & latitudinem novam. Sin majores sint differentiæ, puta graduum 10 vel 20, debebunt observationes quinque adhiberi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When observed changes between successive positions are small (≈4–5°), 3–4 observations suffice for interpolation; for larger changes (≈10–20°) use five observations to achieve reliable interpolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use geometric parabola/chord properties to relate chord segments to times
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma VIII: Si Cometa B moveatur in arcu CBA, & agatur [xi]B secans AC in E: dico quod punctum E abscindet de chorda AC segmentum AE tempori proportionale quamproximè.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit parabolic geometry: a chord segment cut off by a line constructed as described is approximately proportional to the time to describe the corresponding arc. Use this to convert chord segments into time-proportional distances when working with near-parabolic trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate arc by chord using tangent-velocity equivalence (factors 1/3, 2/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma X & Corol.: Cometa quo tempore describit arcum A[mu]C, si progrederetur ea semper cum velocitate quam habet in altitudine ipsi SP æquali, describeret longitudinem æqualem chordæ AC. Corol.: Cometa igitur ea cum velocitate, quam habet in altitudine S[mu] + 2/3I[mu], eodem tempore describeret chordam AC quamproximè.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relating arc lengths and chords for small arcs, replace the actual varying velocity by the velocity at a certain altitude (or at Sμ + (2/3)Iμ) to equate arc travel time to chord traversal approximately. Use the given fractional offsets (1/3, 2/3 of Iμ) per the lemmas to select the appropriate altitude for the equivalent uniform velocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to simpler motion for comparison (falling to Sun thought-experiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma XI: Si Cometa motu omni privatus de altitudine SN seu S[mu] + 1/3I[mu] demitteretur, ut caderet in Solem, & ea semper vi uniformiter continuata urgeretur in Solem qua urgetur sub initio; idem tempore in orbe suo describat arcum AC, descensu suo describeret spatium longitudini I[mu] æquale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use thought experiments that replace actual complex motion with simpler uniform motions (e.g. fall toward Sun) to relate distances and times; these equivalences justify graphical substitutions used in the orbit construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose three observations at nearly equal time intervals with specified spacing condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Seligantur tres observationes æqualibus temporum intervallis ab invicem quamproximè distantes. Sit autem temporis intervallum illud ubi Cometa tardius movetur paulo majus altero, ita videlicet ut temporum differentia sit ad summam temporum ut summa temporum ad dies plus minus sexcentos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer three observations taken at (approximately) equal time intervals. When the comet's motion varies slowly, accept a slight inequality in intervals provided the stated proportionality condition (temporal difference : sum :: sum_of_intervals : ≈600 days) holds; if not available use Lemma VI interpolation with more observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical construction procedure for orbit from three observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prop. XLI construction: choose three observed longitudes TA, tB, τC and construct geometric elements (take a point B on tB, draw BE with ratio to Sagittam tV by the specified relation, draw circumcircle through A,B,C, bisect AC in I, build parallelogram iIλμ, set Isigma = 3 Iλ etc., then derive points X and Z on ecliptic and tangents to obtain two possible comet loci and finally construct parabola with focus S through those loci to get trajectory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the multi-step geometric/graphical construction given (circumcircle, bisect chord, parallelogram constructions, special proportional choices like Iσ = 3 Iλ and adding 3Sσ + 3iλ, iterative redrawing of BE with parts AE & EC proportional to time intervals V & W) to get two candidate comet loci in the plane of the ecliptic; use tangents to latitudes to lift to the comet's true orbit and construct the parabolic trajectory through the computed points. The page gives explicit geometric recipes for each step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose assumed points near the true comet locus and iterate
rubrics_metrics.description: Cæterum puncta B, b, [beta] non quælibet, sed vero proxima eligere convenit. ... Eadem methodo ... inventa sunt, inveniendum erit punctum tertium [beta]; si modò operationem tertiò repetere lubet. Sed hac methodo operationes duæ ut plurimum sufficerint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making assumed constructions (points B, b, β) choose them close to the true comet location; use the computed MP and MN to update assumed points and iterate the construction—typically two iterations suffice unless distances between successive approximations are large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer high-quality repeated measurements to reduce observational error (Flamsteed's method)
rubrics_metrics.description: In his observationibus Flamstedius eâ usus est diligentiâ, ut postquam bis observasset distantiam Cometæ à Stella aliqua fixa, deinde etiam distantiam bis ab alia stella fixa, rediret ad stellam priorem & distantiam Cometæ ab eadem iterum observaret, idque bis, ac deinde ex distantiæ illius incremento vel decremento tempori proportionali colligeret distantiam tempore intermedio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make repeated (paired) measurements of comet-star separations using multiple reference stars, return and remeasure earlier references, and use proportional increments/decrements over time to deduce intermediate separations. This deliberate redundancy reduces random error and improves derived positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument selection and expected precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Hæ observationes Telescopio septupedali, & Micrometro filisque in foco Telescopii locatis paractæ sunt: ... Longitudinum tamen & Latitudinum errores (quatenus ab observationibus nostris oriantur) dimidium minuti unius primi vix superant, præterquam in observatione ultimâ Mart. 9. ubi positiones fixarum ad stellas A & B minus accuratè determinare potui.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a telescope with an attached micrometer (filaments at the focus) for precise position work; under good practice expect longitude and latitude observational errors on the order of ≲0.5' of arc. Note and discount observations where star positions or instrument setup were less accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight observations by observer quality and instrument care
rubrics_metrics.description: His observationibus ... ex his ad operationem primam assumendo tB partium 5657 ... Ex his ad operationem secundam ... Cæterum ... His adde observationes quasdam è nostris. ... Micrometro parum affabre constructâ usus sum, sed Longitudinum tamen & Latitudinum errores ... Cassinus qui Cometam eodem tempore observavit, se declinationem ejus tanquam invariatam manentem parum diligenter definivisse fassus est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer and weight observations from careful observers and well-constructed instruments (Flamsteed, Montenaro, Ango, Nova-Anglia) over cruder records. Note instrument construction defects and declared sloppiness (e.g., Cassini's admission) and treat such observations as less reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate computed orbit by comparing computed and observed positions within expected error margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Tandem ut constaret an Cometa in Orbe sic invento verè moveretur, collegi per operationes partim Arithmeticas partim Graphicas, loca Cometæ in hoc orbe ad observationum quarundam tempora: ... Præterea ... derivabam longitudines & latitudines Cometæ. ... Congruunt igitur observationes tam mense Novembri, quam mensibus tribus subsequentibus cum motu Cometæ circa Solem in Trajectoriâ hacce Parabolicâ, atque adeo hanc esse veram hujus Cometæ Trajectoriam confirmant. Nam differentia inter loca observata & loca computata tam ex erroribus observationum quam ex erroribus operationum Graphicarum in Orbe definiendo admissis, facilè oriri potuere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute predicted longitudes and latitudes from the derived orbit for the times of observations and compare with the observed values. Accept the orbit if discrepancies are consistent with estimated observational and graphical-construction errors; use congruence over multiple months as confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tail-origin hypotheses judged by observed properties (reject optical/refraction accounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cauda nihil aliud sit quam vapor longe tenuissimus, quem caput seu Nucleus Cometæ per calorem suum emittit. Opinio prima (jubaris Solis) est falsa: lux non cernitur quatenus in jubare est, sed quatenus inde reflectitur ad oculos nostros. Opinio secunda (refraction) multi difficultatibus premuntur: Caudæ nunquam variegantur coloribus ... Lux fixarum & planetarum distinctè ad nos transmissa demonstrat medium coeleste nulla vi refractiva pollere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate hypotheses for tail origin by testing against observed facts: tails appear/brighten after perihelion (heating), tails often visible when nucleus is faint, tails are not colored as refracted spectra would be, stars appear through tails (implying rarified medium), tail orientation and curvature correlate with head motion and orbital geometry. These facts favor a vapor-emission/reflecting-particles hypothesis and argue against explanations relying on simple solar rays or atmospheric refraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tail morphology to infer motion and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut quod in planis orbium Cometarum per Solem transeuntibus jacentes, deviant ab oppositione Solis in eas semper partes quas capita in orbibus illis progredientia relinquunt. ... Quod caudæ non deviantes apparent rectæ, deviantes autem incurvantur. Quod curvatura major est ubi major est deviatio, & magis sensibilis ubi cauda cæteris paribus longior est: ... Pendent igitur Phænomena caudæ à motu capitis, non autem à regione coeli in qua caput conspicitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed deviations from exact anti-solar direction, curvature, and brightness asymmetries of the tail to deduce the direction of head motion in its orbital plane and the observer's departure from that plane. Larger deviations and longer tails correlate with greater curvature; convex side tends to be brighter. Interpret tail shape as a dynamical effect, not optical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate cometary atmosphere rarity and sufficiency for tail phenomena by scaling arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Vapores autem, qui spatiis tam immensis implendis sufficiant, ex Cometarum Atmosphæris oriri posse, intelligetur ex raritate aeris nostri. Nam aer juxta superficiem Terræ spatium occupat quasi 850 vicibus majus quam aqua ejusdem ponderis ... inde inveni quod aer, si ascendatur à superficie Terræ ad altitudinem semidiametri unius terrestris, rarior sit quàm apud nos in ratione longe majori ... Proinde ... coma seu Atmosphæra Cometæ, ascendendo ab illius centro, quasi decuplo altior sit quàm superficies nuclei, deinde cauda adhuc altius ascendat, debebit cauda esse quàm rarissima.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply gravitational/pressure scaling (column weight, decrease of density with height and with distance from body center) to estimate that even a very rare atmosphere surrounding a comet nucleus suffices to produce observed tail phenomena; use this to justify visibility of stars through tails and to reject the requirement of dense mediums for tail formation.
